ai.title: Agent templates use TypeScript
ai.summary: Agent templates in .agents/templates/ migrated from JSON to TypeScript. Files like brainstormer.ts, git-committer.ts, and knowledge-keeper.ts now export typed DynamicAgentConfig objects. Loader logic in npm-app/src/agents/load-agents.ts and backend/src/templates/dynamic-agent-service.ts updated to parse TS exports. Zod schemas replace manual JSON definitions for prompt structures.

eli5.text: The AI assistants in this system now define themselves using a more powerful, typed scripting language instead of simple configuration files. If you looked at the folder where assistant profiles live, you would see text files with.ts extensions replacing the old.json files, and their internal definitions now include type-checking tools and schema validation. This affects the core system's assistant profiles, such as the creative brainstorming helper and the automated git commit tool. The change is live today and is already wired into the loaders and templates that the system reads.

ai.title: Fix spawn error in release script
ai.summary: Updated `npm-app/release/index.js` to handle `spawn` failures gracefully. `getCurrentVersion` now returns 'error' string instead of null on missing binary. `main` function wraps binary execution in try/catch, deleting corrupted binaries and retrying download on failure. Update checks now skip if initial spawn errored.

eli5.text: If the helper program that launches your coding assistant gets interrupted while downloading (for example, your computer sleeps or the network drops), the launcher would crash with a confusing spawn error instead of recovering. Now, when that happens, the launcher quietly deletes the half-downloaded file and tries again from scratch, so you don't have to manually reinstall. This only affects the automatic startup process, the assistant itself runs normally once it's successfully launched.

ai.title: Remove console.log from brainstormer template
ai.summary: Removed debug console.log and comment from .agents/templates/brainstormer.ts. Template now contains only agent config logic. Affects agent scaffolding.

eli5.text: A leftover debugging message was cleaned out of one of the starter templates used when building new assistants. As a result, when an assistant is first set up using that template, it will no longer print a stray line of text to the background log, and the template is now ready to contain only the settings needed to define the assistant. The cleanup is in place today and affects only this one template.

eli5.text: You get a small improvement to how models are looked up and how agent templates are handled. The model lookup for caching is now fixed so it correctly identifies which models can be cached, and agent templates have been refactored to use a new step-handling approach. ai.title: Refactor agent tool state to flatten mutableState and add
ai.summary: Flattened `mutableState` into direct state properties (`agentContext`, `messages`, `agentState`) and introduced `getLatestState()` in `CodebuffToolHandlerFunction` across backend tool handlers. Replaced mutable state references with `getFileProcessingValues` in `create-plan.ts` and direct state access in `add-subgoal.ts`, `find-files.ts`, `read-files.ts`, `send-agent-message.ts`, and `spawn-agents-async.ts`. Scope limited to `backend/src/tools/handlers/` and `backend/src/run-agent-step.ts`. `postStreamProcessing` now receives `getLatestState()` output instead of mutable state objects.

eli5.text: The assistant's internal memory system was reorganized so its context is stored more directly instead of through a nested container. This is a behind-the-scenes change affecting how the backend manages agent state during automated tasks. You wouldn't notice any difference in how the assistant behaves, but the system that tracks conversation history and task progress is now structured more simply.

ai.title: Add addmessage and setmessages tools for agent context management
ai.summary: Introduced `add_message` and `set_messages` tools to allow agents to programmatically manipulate conversation history. `add_message` appends a single user or assistant message, while `set_messages` replaces the entire history with a provided array. Both tools are registered in `codebuffToolDefs` and handled via new definitions in `backend/src/tools/definitions/` and handlers in `backend/src/tools/handlers/`. This change modifies `run-agent-step.ts` to rely on the updated message state from these tools rather than manually constructing the final history.

eli5.text: The assistant can now use two new tools to manage the conversation history directly: one adds a single message to the end of the discussion, and the other replaces the entire history with a fresh set of messages. Previously, the system built and adjusted the message list in one central place behind the scenes; now that responsibility is handed over to these tools, so the conversation flow is controlled through them instead of a single hidden routine. This is live today for anyone running the agent step logic.

ai.title: stream-parser guards empty assistant message append
ai.summary: stream-parser.ts now conditionally appends the assistant message to state.messages only when fullResponse is nonempty. Uses buildArray to filter falsy entries, preventing empty message objects from entering history. Affects backend/src/tools/stream-parser.ts.

eli5.text: You probably won't notice this one unless you were looking closely at the logs. When the system finishes building a response, it now checks whether that response actually contains text before saving it to the conversation history, so empty replies no longer create blank entries in past conversations. The change affects how messages are recorded behind the scenes, not what you see on screen.

ai.title: Skip prompt injection on empty user cancellation
ai.summary: Client cancellation logic in npm-app/src/client.ts now conditionally injects the user prompt and system cancellation message only if the prompt is non-empty. Previously, empty prompts resulted in extraneous empty message objects being added to the agent state. This change prevents unnecessary message entries when a user cancels without providing additional input.

eli5.text: When you cancel a response mid-way, the app now only adds a new message to your chat if you actually typed something before canceling. If you hit cancel without typing, it no longer drops a blank message into your conversation. This keeps your chat history clean instead of filling it with empty entries that have no content. The fix is live today in the npm app's client logic.
